title: Dietary emulsifiers impact the mouse gut microbiota promoting colitis and metabolic syndrome
authors: Chassaing B, Koren O, Goodrich JK, Poole AC, Srinivasan S, Ley RE, et al.
population: Wild-type C57BL/6 and Swiss-Webster mice, Il10-deficient and Tlr5-deficient mice, germ-free mice and germ-free recipients of microbiota transplants
funder: This work was supported by NIH grant DK099071 and DK083890. BC is a recipient of the Research Fellowship award from the Crohn's and Colitis Foundation of America (CCFA).
authorConflicts: No statement in the PMC author manuscript.
result: Carboxymethylcellulose or polysorbate 80 at 1.0% in drinking water for 12 weeks reduced the mean distance of the closest bacteria to the epithelium by more than 50% from about 25 µm, raised faecal bioactive flagellin and lipopolysaccharide, caused low-grade inflammation, adiposity and raised fasting glucose in wild-type mice and colitis in Il10- and Tlr5-deficient mice. Germ-free mice were unaffected; microbiota transfer reproduced the effects. Effects appeared from 0.1%. Exposure was not blinded. A 2016 corrigendum (doi 10.1038/nature18000) corrected mouse ages to 5 to 7 weeks and group sizes without changing the conclusions.
